recognize_zh: 高倍周邊血液抹片中多數紅血球周邊有數個長短、粗細不一且間距不規則的尖刺（箭頭），部分細胞緻密缺乏中央淡染區，符合棘狀紅血球（spur cell/acanthocyte）。
features: Red cells with irregularly spaced spicules of unequal length and width, some with knob-like tips (arrows)
Some spiculated cells are dense without central pallor; others retain a central pale zone
Admixed cells with finer, more regular crenation resembling echinocytes
An occasional ovalocyte with preserved central pallor
A neutrophil and scattered platelets in the background
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at high power shows many red cells with irregular, unevenly distributed spicules of variable length and thickness (arrows); several are dense with loss of central pallor. Some cells show finer, more regular projections overlapping with echinocytic change. A neutrophil and platelets are present. Findings are consistent with acanthocytes (spur cells), as seen in spur cell hemolytic anemia of severe liver disease; correlation with liver function is recommended.

ddx.vs: Echinocytes have numerous short, uniform, evenly spaced projections around the whole circumference with central pallor, typical of uremia or drying artifact.
Keratocytes have one or two horn-like projections flanking a ruptured vacuole, as seen in microangiopathic hemolysis, rather than multiple spicules.
These hereditary acanthocytoses are morphologically similar and are separated by Kell antigen testing or lipid studies.
